ca_i_washington_column.blurb: Washington Column is a big granite buttress on the north side of Yosemite Valley, tucked behind the Ahwahnee Hotel and below North Dome. It is among the Valley's busier big-wall objectives, and the routes here mix steep crack climbing with aid. Aid lines outnumber free ones, and the free routes are mostly in the 5.6 to 5.8 range, with a handful in the 5.10 to 5.11 band. Expect long days or overnight ascents on smooth, sustained faces where the rock gets polished and cracks link up the weaknesses. The base is reached on foot from the Valley floor, and the summit can also be gained by an easy trail from the north.

ca_west_face_9.blurb: The West Face is the main climbing wall of Moro Rock, a granite dome beside the Generals Highway near Giant Forest in Sequoia National Park. This is a traditional-protection venue, with about seventeen routes ranging from single pitches to ten-pitch lines. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class at the low end to a few hard 5.12 lines, with the bulk of the climbs at 5.10 and 5.11. Cracks and knobs give the face its character, and it climbs about a thousand vertical feet. It is one of the more convenient big-rock objectives in the park, so the walk from the road is short. Expect serious multi-pitch days rather than quick laps.

ca_sw_face_left_trespassers_wall.blurb: Trespassers Wall is the left-hand section of Little Hunk's southwest face, in the Echo Rock part of central Joshua Tree. Expect delicate, high-angle slab climbing on weathered, orange-tinged rock that can feel crunchy and a bit runout, so composure matters more than raw strength. About seventeen routes are mostly trad, with a few top-ropes and one sport line. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.12, and most of the climbs fall in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. A long diagonal dike gives the wall its signature line. The walk in is short across open desert, and the face stays warm on a chilly afternoon.
ca_sw_face_left_trespassers_wall.approach: From the gravel lot by Echo Rock, follow the trail past the south end of Echo Rock and cross open desert toward the southwest face of Little Hunk. The trail fades near the end; just before the wall, bear right and scramble through brush and boulders to the base.

ca_point_dume.blurb: Point Dume is a small seaside cliff on the Malibu coast in the Santa Monica Mountains, reached from the Pacific Coast Highway. It is mostly a top-rope venue and a popular spot for a first day on real rock. The low-angle west-facing wall holds short, edgy routes around 5.6 to 5.9, ideal for practising footwork, while the seaward south side has a couple of steeper 5.10 lines. A few bolted leads and boulder problems are scattered about, but the fixed gear is not trusted, so bring long anchor cord and top-rope. The setting is scenic, the rock is climbable year-round, and weekdays are quieter.

ca_seven_pines.blurb: Seven Pines is a scatter of boulders in the forest a few miles outside Idyllwild, in the San Jacinto Mountains at roughly 6,300 feet. Reached by a hiking trail, it holds about fifteen boulder problems plus a pair of trad lines. The bouldering ranges from V0 up to V9, with some gentle moderates that make it friendly for climbers just stepping up, and a few hard lines for strong boulderers. The setting is a quiet, shaded mountain hike rather than a roadside crag, so pack your pad in and plan on a low-key session.

ca_pub_wall.blurb: Pub Wall is a compact sport crag in the Central Gorge of the Owens River Gorge near Bishop, set directly beneath the access trail on the climber's left once you reach the canyon floor. All seventeen routes are bolted, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11 and a few easier lines around 5.7 to 5.9, topping out with a hard 5.13 for the strong. It is a great stop for moderate grades and gets early morning sun. Because the gully path runs above the wall, be careful about loose rock, and expect crowds, since the Central Gorge is the busiest part of the canyon.
